american-black-bear: The most common bear in North America, despite often being brown
asiatic-black-bear: Has a pale crescent on its chest; lives from Iran to Japan
brown-bear: Widespread across North America and Eurasia; the coastal Alaskan ones are the largest
polar-bear: The largest land carnivore, hunting seals on Arctic ice
giant-panda: Black and white, and eats almost nothing but bamboo
sloth-bear: A shaggy Indian bear that slurps up termites
sun-bear: The smallest bear, from Southeast Asian rainforests
spectacled-bear: South America's only bear, with pale rings around its eyes
lion: The only truly social cat; males have manes
leopard: A rosette-spotted cat that hauls its kills up trees
jaguar: The Americas' biggest cat, with a crushing bite
snow-leopard: A pale, thick-tailed cat of Central Asia's mountains
rhinoceros: Horned and thick-skinned; comes in black and white
african-elephant: The largest land animal, with big fan-shaped ears
cape-buffalo: A heavy-horned bovine famous for charging hunters
gorilla: The largest primate, living in troops led by a silverback
chimpanzee: Our closest relative along with the bonobo; uses tools
bonobo: A peaceful ape found only south of the Congo River
orangutan: A red-haired tree-dweller of Borneo and Sumatra
